title: Sort files into folders and index them
prompt: Tidy inbox/: move images (.jpg, .png) into images/, documents (.pdf, .docx, .txt) into documents/, and anything else into other/ (all three at the workspace root). Then write index.md with one line per moved file, `- <new path>`, sorted alphabetically. inbox/ should be empty afterwards.

checks.matches:
\A- documents/cv\.docx
- documents/invoice 2026-10\.pdf
- documents/notes\.txt
(?:- images/Logo\.PNG
- images/beach\.jpg|- images/beach\.jpg
- images/Logo\.PNG)
- other/archive\.tar\.gz
- other/song\.mp3\z

notes: Extensions are matched case-insensitively (Logo.PNG is an image). "Sorted alphabetically" has two reasonable readings: plain code-point order (images/Logo.PNG first) and case-insensitive order (images/beach.jpg first). That pair is the only place they differ. The index.md check accepts either order and nothing else, because the whole file must match (\A...\z). The prompt keeps the wording a real user would type, and the grader accepts every valid reading of it.
